purpose: defects in the governed tooling observed while executing R7-0, each with raw evidence, impact, owner and a low-friction fix

findings.observation: the dispatcher refused to dispatch the EXECUTE lane twice because the BRIEF TEXT contained the markers 'git push' and then 'publish' - both inside PROHIBITION sentences ('do not ... '), not in any command. Rewriting the prose to avoid those words let the same lane run.
raw_evidence: the receipt itself prints detection_only=true and says the check cannot stop a lane that writes from inside its own shell
findings.impact: false positives block legitimate bounded writers and tempt operators to weaken briefs (which is worse: a prohibition sentence is exactly what a safe brief SHOULD contain). Detection-only means the guard provides no protection against the attack it names.
findings.fix: match command context, not bare words: require a shell-looking occurrence (e.g. a line beginning with git/gh/curl, or an argv form) and ignore matches inside negative/prohibition sentences; keep detection_only semantics but stop refusing the dispatch on prose.

findings.observation: taskspec_id is derived from the LAST dash segment of the project id, so two projects for the same mission collide on the spine (UNIQUE constraint), and create_workorder resolves git HEAD from the ambient process cwd rather than the project's target_root (ERR_WORKORDER_CRITICAL_FIELD_MISSING when admission runs from a non-repo directory). Three admission attempts were stranded at PLAN_READY as a result.
findings.impact: a governed admission path fails for reasons unrelated to authority, and the failed attempts leave residue in the spine that later readers may misread as real work.
findings.fix: use a full project-id digest (or a spine-wide counter) for taskspec ids, and resolve base_head from the project's target_root instead of cwd; return a typed error instead of inserting a taskspec before the workorder check.

findings.observation: the PIPD product tree is not a git repository, so a bounded writer cannot express its change as a commit or a `git diff`; the WriteSet (path/bytes/sha256 + pre-hash) and a unified diff produced with `diff -u` / `git diff --no-index` are the only reproducibility handle.
findings.impact: reviewers cannot rely on git-provided provenance for product changes in this tree; the WriteSet digest becomes the binding.
findings.fix: either place the product under version control or require the WriteSet+diff pair as the standing convention for this tree (the R7-0 writer receipt follows the latter).
findings.owner: PIPD Product Owner / Fabric Repo Maintainer

findings.observation: a credential-shaped literal inside a script line (an authorization header written from an f-string) is rendered back to the operator as 'Bearer ***'. Reading the file directly (bytes) shows the real placeholder, so the display is a redaction, not the file content - it can mislead an operator into 'repairing' a working line.
raw_evidence: operator observed the redacted rendering, then confirmed the on-disk bytes with a byte-level read
findings.impact: wasted edit cycles and a risk of corrupting working code; no integrity impact.
findings.fix: none required in the product; note it in the operating guidance (verify bytes before editing secret-adjacent lines).

findings.title: Product test suite depends on a git ref the product tree does not have
findings.observation: tests/test_publication_projection.py and tests/test_tooling_executes.py fail with "cannot resolve ref 'r5-s4-candidate' in C:/Projects/Agent_Workspace/PIPD/.git"; the full suite reports 7 failed / 319 passed / 2 skipped.
findings.impact: A regression signal is unusable as-is: a reader cannot tell pre-existing environment failures from change-induced ones without a baseline run.
findings.remediation: Make the suite skip (not fail) when the required ref is absent, or provide the ref in the fixture. Checker is separately required to classify the 7 as pre-existing vs introduced. Owner: PIPD tooling.

findings.title: Recurring nonce-carrier verdict defect on Codex-CLI lanes
findings.observation: Attempt 3 also returned ok=false ERR_NO_ARM_EMITTED_NONCE with usage_receipt_ok=true and nonce_absent_arms=[opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash] (attempts 1-2 in R6R7 showed the same shape, and the VERIFY lane showed it for opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash).
findings.impact: The dispatcher cannot positively attest the served arm from its own evidence, so model attribution rests on recorded usage rows rather than a nonce.
findings.remediation: Fix the nonce emission/echo path in the relay or the wrapper so require==served can be shown, instead of continuing to record WARNs. Owner: HG-KSEOS lane tooling.

findings.title: Checker lane voids its own verdict when a re-run driver writes in place over the guarded subject
findings.observation: VERIFY_SECURITY attempt 1 produced a full review, then the dispatcher returned ERR_CHECKER_MUTATED_SUBJECT (changed=14, removed=0): the re-run of the mutation driver wrote RAW/mut_m*.json + RUNNERS/mutation_records.json in place inside the guarded subject R6_DELIVERY/, i.e. over the writer's frozen receipts. The guard behaved correctly; the lane self-voided.
findings.impact: A void verdict costs a full lane turn (22 min) and, worse, silently drifts a frozen evidence tree in the workspace unless someone restores it. The drift was repaired byte-for-byte from the merged packet (recorded in R6_DELIVERY_RAW_RESTORE.json).
findings.remediation: (a) The dispatch brief for a checker must state a writable output root OUTSIDE every guarded subject and forbid writes into the subject (now done); (b) give the mutation driver an explicit --out-dir so a re-run never defaults into the frozen tree; (c) print the guarded subject paths in the brief so the lane can see them. Owner: HG-KSEOS lane tooling + PIPD driver.

findings.title: Guard subject includes VCS-ignored byproducts, so routine hygiene can void a verdict
findings.observation: VERIFY_SECURITY attempt 2 was voided with changed=0 removed=1: the removed path was the gitignored byproduct R6_DELIVERY/RUNNERS/__pycache__/probe_lib.cpython-311.pyc, deleted out-of-band by the orchestrator after the checker's own turn. The checker's own conduct in that turn was clean (added=0, changed=0).
findings.impact: A lane's verdict can be voided by an event it neither caused nor can see. Two of this round's three checker attempts were voided this way or similarly (attempt 1 by the lane's own in-place re-run), which is 50+ minutes of lane budget spent on receipt plumbing rather than verification.
findings.remediation: (a) Define the guarded subject as the tracked (packet) file set, or normalise VCS-ignored byproducts out of it before the turn opens and keep them out; (b) treat ignored paths as 'added/removed, not fatal, recorded' instead of voiding; (c) state in the dispatch brief that the guard covers ignored byproducts. Owner: HG-KSEOS lane tooling.

findings.title: Guard compares end-state only, so a lane can write into the subject and restore it without being caught; the driver keeps defaulting its output into the frozen tree
findings.observation: During VERIFY_SECURITY attempt 3 the mutation driver again wrote 13 RAW receipts in place into the guarded subject R6_DELIVERY (23:28 local). The checker detected it, restored the bytes from the merged git blobs itself, and disclosed it as a boundary violation. The dispatcher's guard reported CLEAN (added=0 removed=0 changed=0) because it compares the subject digest before vs after the turn only. Third occurrence of the in-place-driver-write class this round (attempt 1 fatal, attempt 2 orchestrator-caused, attempt 3 self-detected and repaired).
findings.impact: The guard cannot see intra-turn writes, so 'CLEAN' is weaker than it looks; the only reason the frozen bytes survived is that the lane chose to repair and disclose. Two of three checker attempts were spent on this class of problem.
findings.remediation: (a) add --out-dir/DEST to probe_mutations.py so a re-run writes where it is told; (b) sample the subject digest during the turn (or use a read-only mount / deny ACE for the duration) instead of comparing end states; (c) keep the disclosure requirement in the brief (it worked). Owner: PIPD tooling (a) + HG-KSEOS lane tooling (b).

findings.title: self-check harness expectations are snapshotted, so they go stale after every packet commit
findings.detail: round_selfcheck.py compares the live packet against recorded readback blobs/manifest from an earlier commit; after the packet grew 212 -> 227 blobs the harness returned 1=PASS 2=FAIL 3=FAIL 4=PASS 5=PASS 6=PASS (OVERALL FAIL) instead of silently passing. The refusal is correct behaviour, but the recorded expectation source is the wrong one.
findings.fix: derive expectations from the live manifest/tree at run time (or regenerate them as an explicit step of the publish pipeline) so a green run means 'the packet equals its own manifest', not 'the packet equals an old snapshot'.

claim_ceiling: LOCAL observation; not a product defect verdict
